title: Initial Modifiers: Match the Noun After the Comma
description: Identify an opening modifier, predict the noun phrase it describes or compares, and choose the answer that places that noun phrase immediately after the comma.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Mechanic Asha inspected a bicycle immediately after its rider reported a clicking noise. Checking the wheel for cracks, ______
questions.explanation_html: Asha checks the wheel. Her name must come immediately after the opening action.
questions.variation: Place the doer of an opening action after the comma
choices: a split near the hub drew Asha’s attention.
the clicking noise prompted Asha to inspect the bike.
Asha noticed a split near the hub.
the rider’s bicycle was found to have a split.

distractor_notes.A: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.B: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.D: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: After collecting the seed sample, the botanists sealed it inside an airtight container. Sealed inside an airtight container, ______
questions.explanation_html: The seed sample is sealed inside the container. It belongs directly after the comma.
questions.variation: Place the noun in the stated condition after the comma
choices: the botanists took the seed sample to a second lab.
the seed sample remained dry during transport.
the container kept the sample dry.
transport between the two labs took a day.

distractor_notes.A: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.C: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.D: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: A yellow buoy floats near the inlet. Bright against the gray water, ______
questions.explanation_html: The buoy is the bright object. Put it after the comma.
questions.variation: Match a noun to an opening description without a verb
choices: the buoy marks the edge of the channel.
the inlet has a buoy marking the channel.
the channel is marked by a yellow buoy.
the harbor crew installed a yellow buoy.

distractor_notes.B: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.C: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.D: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: A lab compared the water absorption of a cloth and a foam. The cloth absorbed twice as much water as the foam. Unlike that of the foam, ______
questions.explanation_html: “That” refers to water absorption. The comparison needs the cloth’s water absorption immediately after the comma.
questions.variation: Compare the same property rather than the things that have it
choices: the cloth’s water absorption was relatively high.
the cloth took up a large amount of water.
the lab measured a large amount of water absorbed by the cloth.
the water was taken up more readily by the cloth.

distractor_notes.B: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.C: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.D: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Artist Leo made the decision to finish the mural that day. His assistants brought paint but did not work on the wall. Determined to finish the mural before sunset, ______
questions.explanation_html: Leo is determined. A passive version that names the mural first makes the modifier attach to the wrong noun.
questions.variation: Use the first noun position even when the rest of each choice is plausible
choices: the mural was painted without a break by Leo.
sunset approached as Leo painted.
his assistants brought Leo an extra can of paint.
Leo painted without taking a break.

distractor_notes.A: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.B: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.C: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Javier received a letter from his great-aunt. He used a desk lamp to read it. Reading the faded paper under a lamp, ______
questions.explanation_html: Javier reads the letter. The opening phrase modifies him, not the objects in the scene.
questions.variation: Place the doer of an opening action after the comma
choices: a list of names caught Javier’s attention.
the faded letter contained a list of names.
Javier found a list of names.
a desk lamp helped Javier find a name.

questions.stimulus_html: Hikers Maya and Leif completed a steep ascent. The park ranger met them at the summit after taking a service road. Exhausted by the climb, ______

questions.variation: Place the noun in the stated condition after the comma
choices: the park ranger met the pair at the summit.
Maya and Leif took a long rest.
a long rest appealed to the two hikers.
the steep ascent ended near a shelter.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: A wren, a dove, and two finches live in the aviary. The wren is smaller than all the others. The smallest bird in the aviary, ______
questions.explanation_html: The description names the wren, so the sentence must begin its main clause with the wren.
questions.variation: Match a noun to an opening description without a verb
choices: the aviary houses a wren.
the wren often perches beside the door.
the door has a perch used by the wren.
a keeper sometimes sees the wren at the door.

distractor_notes.A: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.C: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.
distractor_notes.D: The noun immediately after the comma does not match what the opening phrase describes.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The experiment compared the thermal expansion of an aluminum rod and a brass rod. The aluminum rod lengthened more. Compared with that of the brass rod, ______
questions.explanation_html: Compare thermal expansion to thermal expansion. The correct choice names the aluminum rod’s property first.
questions.variation: Compare the same property rather than the things that have it
choices: the thermal expansion of the aluminum rod was greater.
the aluminum rod lengthened more.
the experiment found that aluminum lengthened more.
a greater change in length was recorded for aluminum.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Dana searched the room but could not see into the far corners. Unable to locate the key in the dark, ______
questions.explanation_html: Dana is unable to locate the key. The flashlight, corners, and key are objects rather than the searcher.
questions.variation: Use the first noun position even when the rest of each choice is plausible
choices: a flashlight helped Dana see the corners.
the corners were lit by Dana’s flashlight.
the key became visible when Dana used a light.
Dana turned on a flashlight.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Tuner Nia installed and played each string while the violin’s owner listened. Testing the sound of each replacement string, ______
questions.explanation_html: Nia is the person doing the testing, so only the sentence beginning with her name attaches the action to its doer.
questions.variation: Place the doer of an opening action after the comma
choices: one string sounded lower to Nia.
the violin’s owner heard an unexpectedly deep note.
Nia discovered that one string was a little too thick.
the sound of the thickest string surprised the owner.

questions.stimulus_html: The builder mounted two braces below the floor of the loft. Mounted below the loft floor, ______
questions.explanation_html: The braces are mounted below the floor. Only the correct construction puts them right after the modifier.
questions.variation: Place the noun in the stated condition after the comma

the builder reinforced the wooden boards.
the braces supported its wooden boards.
the loft floor felt more stable.

questions.stimulus_html: A dark reef is submerged at high tide, and swimmers can almost never see it from the shore. Barely visible from shore, ______

choices: the mouth of the bay contains a reef.
the dark reef extends across the mouth of the bay.
swimmers rarely see the dark reef.
the shoreline curves around a submerged reef.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The needle lengths of a spruce and a fir were measured. The fir’s needles were longer on average. Unlike those of the spruce, ______
questions.explanation_html: “Those” refers to needle lengths. The first noun phrase must name the other group of needle lengths.
questions.variation: Compare the same property rather than the things that have it
choices: the needle lengths of the fir were greater on average.
the fir was found to have longer needles.
the two species differed in their needle lengths.
the researchers found that the fir had longer needles.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Acoustics researcher Sol compared the tones personally while an assistant recorded the readings. Comparing the tones at several volumes, ______
questions.explanation_html: Sol made the comparison. Only the active phrasing makes Sol the immediate noun following the opening modifier.
questions.variation: Use the first noun position even when the rest of each choice is plausible
choices: a faint ringing sound was identified by Sol.
the readings were recorded by Sol’s assistant.
a louder tone made a faint ring audible to Sol.
Sol identified a faint ringing sound at the higher settings.
